Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear examples, that helps. Short answer: we bill input + output tokens for each request, but there are a couple of important operational layers that affect the invoice total. I wanted to loop Jordan (SE) and our pricing lead Vivek into the thread so we can give you both a technical and commercial view.

High-level bullets:
- Base meter: input tokens + output tokens (same as you suspected).
- Rounding quantum: by default we round per-call charges up to the nearest 16-token increment for efficiency; e.g., a 53-token call -> billed as 64 tokens.
- Minimum per-call floor: there is an optional per-call floor applied for some committed SKUs (default hosted API has NO per-call floor; committed enterprise SKUs can include a 128-token per-call minimum to simplify forecasting).
- Session/KB reuse: we maintain per-conversation KV caching. If two calls reuse an identical prefix within the same active conversation window (30s–5min depending on heartbeat) the prefix cost is NOT charged twice for the generation portion; however input tokens are still counted on the call that transmits them.
- Long responses: generation tokens are billed at the same unit rate as short responses, but for long outputs you can configure fallback to a chunked streaming mode which can reduce rounding overhead for very long replies.

I'll let Jordan and Vivek add technical examples and propose a small sample invoice you can drop into Procurement.

A quick technical/numbered breakdown (feel free to paste into the one-sheet):

1) Rounding behavior
- We round each call to the nearest 16-token increment. So 420 -> 432, 32 -> 32, 53 -> 64.

2) Example A (device heartbeat)
- Input 32 (billed 32) + output 420 (billed 432) = 464 billed tokens per call.

3) Prefix reuse rules
- Active conversation window: by default 2 minutes of activity keeps KV cached for that conversation (configurable per account). If the second micro-session is within that window AND uses the same conversation id, generation reuse prevents re-sending the prefix as new generation tokens. Practically: the second call still transmits input tokens (so those are billed) but the generation kernel can reuse cached KV for the prefix so generation tokens attributable to the prefix are not double-billed.
- In your Example B: prefix 20 tokens appears twice. Atlas will be charged for the 30-token prompt input each time, and for generation tokens produced; the part of generation that is the cached prefix is not recharged. So it's not a strict 2x in many cases.

4) Long-response streaming and chunking
- For >1k-token responses we can enable streaming chunking which reduces rounding overhead: charges are applied per-chunk (each chunk rounded), and for very large responses this typically reduces excess rounding relative to a single large rounded bucket.

5) Quick cost calc (assume unit price $0.0008 / token for generation, $0.0004 / token for input - example enterprise rates):
- Per-token mode: 120k calls * (avg input 35 + avg output 600) = 120k * 635 = 76,200,000 tokens * blended unit ~ $0.0007 => $53,340 monthly. (This includes rounding estimate: +4% overhead due to 16-token rounding and chunking inefficiencies.)
- Slab (128 per-call floor) with 10% committed discount: billed tokens per call = max(128, 635) = 635 => same as above for this workload, so slab only hurts if average call falls below 128. For micro-session heavy workloads it can be worse.

6) Recommendation:
- For Atlas' profile (avg output 600) a per-token model with our 16-token rounding is likely lower. However if they have a significant tail of short calls (device heartbeats) we should offer a temporary concession: 3-month pilot where we waive the per-call floor for committed customers or provide a small monthly credit to offset rounding inefficiency.
